Subject: Solstice AI private deployment kickoff — preflight & egress policy

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for the private deployment. I’m Sofia (CSM) and I’ll be your primary point for onboarding. We want to make the networking cutover as low-risk as possible — below is a suggested agenda for the preflight phase and a couple of asks to unblock our infra team.

Planned preflight agenda (week of Aug 10):
- Review network topology and peering approach (AWS TGW vs VPC peering)
- Confirm private endpoint coverage (Tokens, control-plane, telemetry)
- Egress policy: allowlist vs forced egress through customer NAT/private proxy
- On‑prem package planning (installer access, air-gap considerations)
- Cutover weekend windows and rollback criteria

Immediate asks for your network team:
1) Confirm preferred peering method (TGW preferred for multi-account) and the AWS accounts we should attach.
2) Share the VPC CIDR(s) and any IP ranges reserved for private endpoints.
3) Confirm whether outbound internet egress will be allowed from the Redwood pods (NAT) or must be blocked/proxied — if blocked, do you have a private proxy or firewall that will perform TLS inspection?

Attached: vpc-diagram-solstice.pdf and solstice-map-ownership.xlsx (mutual action plan).

If you’re available, can we book a 30 min tech preflight on Aug 11 or Aug 12? I’ve copied Aditya (networking) and Grace (deploy lead) — they’ll handle the technical checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova

Hi Sofia —

Appreciate the clear agenda. Quick answers from our side:
- We prefer AWS Transit Gateway (TGW) for the peering (multi-account).
- Attaching network lead: Carlos Mendez (cc’d). Procurement/contract questions are with J. Patel (cc’d).
- Proposed maintenance window: Aug 19 22:00 UTC — Aug 20 04:00 UTC (we can be flexible if that conflicts).

Subject: Re: Solstice AI private deployment kickoff — preflight & egress policy

Elena / Carlos —

Thanks for the inventory — that helps. A few technical clarifications before the tech sync:

1) CIDR details: I see 10.20.0.0/16 listed; you mentioned reserving 10.20.50.0/24 for endpoints. Can you confirm the exact /24(s) we should allocate for: control-plane endpoints, telemetry, and optional model artifacts? We recommend keeping separate /24 blocks to simplify firewall rules.

2) Egress behavior: Redwood can be configured two ways:
   - Option A (simpler): We route telemetry and image checks over the customer NAT (outbound). Requires outbound HTTPS to known endpoints; we will provide IP ranges and FQDNs.
   - Option B (private-only): We expose private endpoints inside your VPC and all control-plane traffic stays private. This requires the VPC to accept our ENIs and the TGW attachment rules to allow the specific /24s.

3) TLS inspection: If you perform TLS interception and re-sign certificates, that will interfere with our installer and image verification (we verify signatures end-to-end). For air-gapped/inspection scenarios we can provide signed offline installers, but that changes the cutover approach.

4) On‑prem package: Please confirm whether your security team requires HSM/KMS integration for key storage for the on‑prem package or if customer-managed KMS is preferred.

For the Aug 11 sync (16:00 UTC) — proposed attendees: Sofia, Aditya, me, Carlos, and one person from your security team who can answer the TLS/inspection question.

– Grace
Grace Oconnor
Deploy Lead, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

Team —

Thanks for the quick responses. I’ve put together a short preflight checklist and a proposed cutover runbook (attached). Summary and immediate asks below so the Aug 11 sync can be strictly technical:

Preflight checklist (items to confirm before cutover):
1) TGW Attachments: please confirm AWS account IDs for the two VPCs to attach and the TGW owner account.
2) Endpoint CIDRs: confirm the final /24s for control-plane, telemetry, and artifacts.
3) Egress model: confirm Option A (customer NAT) or Option B (private-only). If Option A, provide EIP/NAT IPs we should allow. If Option B, ensure TGW policies allow our endpoint /24s.
4) TLS interception: if present, please confirm whether you can provide a security contact for an offline installer path (we ship signed installers for that case).
5) KMS: confirm whether Solstice will provide a CMK (customer-managed key) or use Redwood-managed keys for bundle encryption.
6) Firewall rules: provide the CIDR/IP allowlist (we included a template in the attachment).

Cutover runbook highlights (attached doc):
- Pre-cutover validation (connectivity tests, DNS override checks, private endpoint handshake)
- Cutover steps (TGW attach, route propagation, private endpoint DNS switch, failover test)
- Rollback triggers (failed handshake, >5% request error rate after 10m, auth failures)
- Post-cutover validation (per-route latency checks, token exchange validation)

Immediate asks for Solstice before Aug 11 sync:
- Confirm TGW account IDs and final endpoint CIDRs (1–2 business days preferred).
- Confirm whether TLS interception is in scope (we can provide an offline install if so).
- Confirm security contact for KMS discussion (name + email).

Proposed tech sync: Aug 11, 2026 at 16:00 UTC — meeting link: https://zoom.us/j/0000000000 (please confirm).

Attachments: private-deploy-cutover-runbook.docx, firewall-rule-template.csv

If we get the above, we’ll finalize the MAP and lock the cutover window (targeting Aug 19 as discussed).

Best,
Aditya Rao
